messages.subject: legend control on develop branch
parts:
I have a data set that has statistical uncertainties (which I'm using geom_pointrange to represent) and associated systematic uncertainties (for which I'm using geom_ribbon).  I wouldn't be surprised if there are better ways to achieve what I'm trying to do, but the code at the end of this post gives you an idea of what I'm working with right now.  I specify "legend = FALSE" for the geom_ribbon, as the correspondence of color makes it clear which ribbon goes with which data points.  In 0.8.9 this works and I don't end up with a legend entry for the ribbon.  On the develop branch, however, the ribbon legend shows up no matter what I do.

My main question: is there a way to turn off unwanted legends on the develop branch?

Some other questions related to what I'm trying to do.  Is there a better "ggplot2 way" of plotting these two pieces of information together (i.e., the statistical and systematic uncertainties)?  Maybe some way of using stat_summary? It took a bit of work to get the color of the points and the ribbon properly synchronized - is there a better way to do that?  

- Dave

x<-1:10
y<-2*x
e<-0.05*y
s<-0.1*y
t<-0
d0<-data.frame(x,y,e,s,t)
y<-20/x
e<-0.05*y
s<-0.1*y
t<-1
d1<-data.frame(x,y,e,s,t)
d<-rbind(d0,d1)
print(ggplot(d) + theme_bw() +
    opts(legend.position=c(0.4,0.8),legend.direction="vertical") +
    geom_ribbon(aes(x=x,ymin=y-s,ymax=y+s,group=t,fill=factor(t)),alpha=0.6,legend=FALSE) +
    geom_pointrange(aes(x=x,y=y,ymin=y-e,ymax=y+e,shape=factor(t),colour=factor(t)),size=0.6,fill="white") +
    scale_shape_manual("legend",values=c(19,21),breaks=c(0,1)) +
    scale_color_manual("legend",values=c("red","blue"),breaks=c(0,1)))

I'm not using the develop branch, so I'm can't check this, but I'm
surprised you can disable the legend in the geom call at all. Legends
are associated with scales, not geoms, so I always thought you had to
set legend = false in the scale call. Try scale_fill_hue(legend =
FALSE) and see if that works.

>

> ribbon properly synchronized - is there a better way to do that?

what about something like

d$t <- factor(d$t) # Only need to do this once.

ggplot(d, aes(x = x, y = y, shape = t, colour = t, fill = t)) +
geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=y-s, ymax=y+s), alpha = 0.6) +
geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = y-e, ymax = y+e), size=0.6, fill="white") +
scale_fill_hue(legend = FALSE) +

theme_bw() +
opts(legend.position=c(0.4,0.8),legend.direction="vertical")

messages.subject: Re: legend control on develop branch
parts:
Hi Ista,

Thanks! Super tips on all counts.

On Sunday, July 10, 2011 12:05:49 PM UTC-4, Ista Zahn wrote:

I'm not using the develop branch, so I'm can't check this, but I'm
surprised you can disable the legend in the geom call at all. Legends
are associated with scales, not geoms, so I always thought you had to
set legend = false in the scale call. Try scale_fill_hue(legend =
FALSE) and see if that works.
Works like a charm.  This clearly represents a conceptual problem on my end.  I guess I hadn't quite grokked the ggplot factorization into geoms, scales and coords as well as I thought I had.

what about something like

d$t <- factor(d$t) # Only need to do this once.
Nice.  Works.

ggplot(d, aes(x = x, y = y, shape = t, colour = t, fill = t)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=y-s, ymax=y+s), alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = y-e, ymax = y+e), size=0.6, fill="white") +
  scale_fill_hue(legend = FALSE) +
  theme_bw() +
  opts(legend.position=c(0.4,0.8),legend.direction="vertical")
I went with the code below and got just what I was hoping for.

print(ggplot(d) + theme_bw() +
    opts(legend.position=c(0.4,0.8),legend.direction="vertical") +

geom_ribbon(aes(x=x,ymin=y-s,ymax=y+s,group=t,fill=t),alpha=0.3) +
    geom_pointrange(aes(x=x,y=y,ymin=y-e,ymax=y+e,shape=t,colour=t),size=0.6,fill="white") +
    scale_fill_manual("",values=c("blue","red"),breaks=c(0,1),legend=FALSE) +
    scale_shape_manual("legend",values=c(19,21),breaks=c(0,1)) +
    scale_color_manual("legend",values=c("blue","red"),breaks=c(0,1)))

Thanks!

- Dave

messages.subject: Re: legend control on develop branch
parts: I may have declared victory a little too soon.  With this code

x<-1:10
y<-2*x

t<-0
d0<-data.frame(x,y,t)
y<-20/x
t<-1
d1<-data.frame(x,y,t)
d<-rbind(d0,d1)
d$t=factor(d$t)
print(ggplot(d) + theme_bw() +
    geom_point(aes(x=x,y=y,color=factor(t)),pch=19) +
    scale_color_hue("legend",labels=c("a","b"),breaks=c(0,1)))

I end up with the plot I'd expect -  a legend with a title "legend" and labels "a" and "b".  If I try and specify things myself, however, using scale_color_manual, like this:

x<-1:10
y<-2*x

t<-0
d0<-data.frame(x,y,t)
y<-20/x
t<-1
d1<-data.frame(x,y,t)
d<-rbind(d0,d1)
d$t=factor(d$t)
print(ggplot(d) + theme_bw() +
    geom_point(aes(x=x,y=y,color=factor(t)),pch=19) +
    scale_color_manual(name = "legend",values = c("blue", "red"), labels=c("a","b"),breaks=c(0,1)))

I end up with a legend entitled "factor(t)" and labels "0" and "1".  Not what I was hoping for.  I poked around in scale-manual.r, compared it to scale-hue.r, and if I make this change:

--- scale-manual.r.orig 2011-07-10 23:33:59.000000000 -0400
+++ scale-manual.r      2011-07-10 23:34:13.000000000 -0400
@@ -24,7 +24,7 @@
 #' p + scale_colour_manual(values = cols, limits = c("4", "8"))
 #' p + scale_colour_manual(values = cols, limits = c("4", "6", "8", "10"))
 scale_colour_manual <- function(..., values) {
-  discrete_scale("colour", "manual", manual_pal(values))
+  discrete_scale("colour", "manual", manual_pal(values), ...)
 }
 
 #' @rdname scale_manual

That is, I add the ellipsis parameter to the call to discrete_scale, then I get a legend with the name and labels I expected.  Perhaps someone with more expertise could comment - do the various "scale_xxx_manual" functions need some tweaking to pass along titles and labels and such?  

- Dave
